# The eight approaches as design methodologies

Each approach is a complete way of designing a site, not a set of sections. A site follows one, as a whole. Another approach joins only when the methodology lists it under "Combines with", the direction gives a written reason, and the operator approves it at B2.

The "From the team" lines come from the Master Review workbook and the approach skills. The "Interpretation" lines are harness authors' reading and should be checked against Nidhi's approach definitions.

## APP-01 AI to Full Website

Words and structure carry the site. A complete multi-page website whose distinction comes from typography, editorial composition and real content, not from effects.

**Principles**

- The client's real words are the design material
- Type and white space create hierarchy before any decoration
- Every page has one job and one call to action
- Fast and accessible is part of the look

**Visual identity:** Editorial and confident, like a well-made printed brochure. A strong type voice, a restrained palette, one signature graphic device repeated across pages.

**Art direction:** Choose one graphic device (a rule system, numbered margins, an oversized initial, a photo crop) and use it everywhere. Photography is art-directed and cropped with intent, never decorative stock filler.

**Layout and composition:** An asymmetric grid with real tension: wide margins, offset columns, images that break the column, sections of different heights and densities. Cards only where items are truly equal. Patterns: `editorial-split`, `asymmetric`, `full-bleed`, `overlap`, `list-editorial`, `quote-feature`, `stats-band`, `statement`.

**Typography:** A distinctive display face at large sizes against a readable body face. At least five clear levels. Headline size and measure do the work other approaches give to motion.

**Colour:** Light by default. One primary, one accent used at most twice per screen, large neutral surfaces. Colour blocks mark changes of topic.

**Content:** Long enough to persuade. Real headlines with a point of view, specific service detail, proof with sources, plain calls to action. Prose is laid out, not dumped.

**Images and assets:** Client or licensed photography, cropped to a consistent treatment. Authored SVG diagrams or marks where photos do not exist. No placeholder art in a finished site.

**Animation and interaction:** Quiet: CSS reveals on entry, hover states that confirm a link, one small signature micro-interaction. Nothing that delays reading.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Native scrolling. No pinning, no smooth-scroll library, no scroll hijack. Page transitions may use the browser View Transitions API.

**Responsive:** Rebuild the composition for mobile instead of stacking it: reorder so the point comes first, keep display type large, keep the graphic device. Tablet keeps two columns where the measure allows.

**Use for:** Service businesses; Marketing sites; Nonprofits; Any project where content and speed matter most; The fallback for every other approach

**Avoid for:** A launch whose point is a staged story; A product that must be turned over in 3D

**Combines with:** nothing

**The render check requires:** nothing special; forbids pinned, webgl

**From the team:** Workbook: end-to-end AI build, first version looked plain, client-approved 7-page site with a content lock (Nidhi). Skill: base build method on the starter

**Interpretation:** Philosophy, editorial composition rules, signature device

## APP-02 Cinematic Scroll Website

The page is a film and the visitor holds the playhead. Scroll is time: every section is a scene with an entrance, a beat and an exit, telling one story from start to finish.

**Principles**

- One narrative arc across the page, not a list of sections
- Scroll position drives motion, so the visitor stays in control
- Each scene has a single idea and a single focal point
- A still frame of any scene should look composed

**Visual identity:** Cinematic: full-viewport scenes, strong contrast, big type treated as an image, dramatic scale changes and letterbox-like framing.

**Art direction:** Think in shots: establishing shot, close-up, reveal, closing shot. A consistent light and colour grade across imagery. One recurring visual motif carries through the scenes.

**Layout and composition:** Full-height scenes composed around one focal point, with type and image overlapping. A pinned horizontal strip or stepped sequence for the central part of the story. Almost no card grids. Patterns: `full-bleed`, `pinned-scene`, `horizontal-story`, `scene-stack`, `statement`, `overlap`, `chapter-opener`.

**Typography:** Very large display type with tight leading, revealed line by line. Short lines. Body copy is sparse and placed like subtitles.

**Colour:** A controlled grade that may shift by scene: dark scenes are allowed when the story earns them, with palette changes used as chapter breaks.

**Content:** Script, not brochure: short lines in sequence, one idea per scene, the product or offer revealed after the story sets it up, a closing scene with the call to action.

**Images and assets:** Large, high-quality stills or video with room for type. Video needs dense keyframes for scrubbing (the team hit lag with 2 keyframes in 241 frames). Authored vector scenes are fine when they have depth and layers.

**Animation and interaction:** GSAP ScrollTrigger timelines: scrubbed reveals, pinned scenes, parallax between layers, split-line headlines, colour transitions between chapters. Motion always explains the story order.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Lenis smooth scroll synced to ScrollTrigger. At least one pinned scene and one scrubbed sequence. Never trap the visitor: scenes end on their own and a skip is always possible by scrolling.

**Responsive:** Scenes stay full height on mobile with recomposed framing. Horizontal strips become vertical steps or swipe. Reduced motion shows the stacked static layout with every word readable.

**Use for:** Product launches; Brand stories; Premium business sites with a story to tell

**Avoid for:** Information-heavy service sites; Low-motion or low-end-device audiences

**Combines with:** APP-05 (One shader scene is itself a chapter of the story); APP-08 (A frame sequence is the central scrubbed scene)

**The render check requires:** pinned; forbids webgl

**From the team:** Workbook: narrative storytelling with scrubbed timelines; 9-scene journey, pinned horizontal services strip, scrubbed product video, door transition, palette drift and sync issues. Skill: pinned ScrollStory and Chapter sections, GSAP, Lenis, fallbacks

**Interpretation:** Film language, shot thinking, script-style copy

## APP-03 Interactive 3D Website

The product is an object you can handle. The site is a showroom built around one 3D subject, and interaction replaces description.

**Principles**

- One hero object, not a scene full of things
- Touching it teaches something: each interaction reveals a real feature
- The poster must already sell it before WebGL loads
- Interface stays out of the way of the object

**Visual identity:** A studio: clean stage, controlled lighting, generous negative space, interface labels that attach to the object like annotations.

**Art direction:** Direct the object like a product shoot: lighting, material, camera angles chosen per section. The page background is the studio backdrop.

**Layout and composition:** The object anchors the composition and moves between sections, with text placed around it. Few, large sections. Patterns: `object-stage`, `annotated-object`, `full-bleed`, `editorial-split`, `statement`.

**Typography:** Precise and technical: clean display type with small annotation labels, numerals for specifications.

**Colour:** Neutral stage colours that make the object's material the richest thing on the page.

**Content:** Short feature statements tied to parts of the object, then a specification list and a call to action.

**Images and assets:** A licensed or authored glTF model under 3 MB with a poster for every scene. Procedural geometry is allowed when it is on purpose.

**Animation and interaction:** Drag or orbit, camera moves tied to scroll, hotspots that focus the camera. Idle motion is subtle.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Native scroll drives camera interpolation between saved views.

**Responsive:** Mobile keeps the object with touch rotation or falls to the poster. Profile mobile: the team removed 3D for stutter on one site.

**Use for:** Showrooms; Physical products; Data shown as a spatial object

**Avoid for:** Low-end device floors; Service businesses with no object

**Combines with:** APP-02 (The story needs pinned chapters around the object; use APP-07 for a flagship)

**The render check requires:** webgl; forbids nothing

**From the team:** Workbook: real-time 3D with cursor and camera; scroll-driven camera, lazy GLB, HTML overlays synced to scroll; mobile unprofiled. Skill: Scene3D behind a poster

**Interpretation:** Studio art direction, one-object rule

## APP-04 Spline + Website

A designer-made micro 3D moment adds delight to a clear product page. The scene decorates and demonstrates; the page does the explaining.

**Principles**

- One small scene with one purpose
- Page and scene talk to each other through events
- The scene is edited visually, by a designer
- The page works fully without it

**Visual identity:** Friendly, tactile SaaS: soft shapes, gentle materials, a playful object matched to a crisp interface.

**Art direction:** Match the scene's colours and material to the design system. Keep the object toy-like and simple.

**Layout and composition:** A product page with a hero or feature visual slot holding the scene. Feature blocks may vary in size; a bento grid is on-style here when items differ. Patterns: `editorial-split`, `statement`, `feature-demo`, `bento`, `full-bleed`.

**Typography:** Friendly modern sans at clear sizes, with tight headlines and short sentences.

**Colour:** Bright, friendly accents from the scene carried into interface details.

**Content:** Clear product marketing: what it does, how it works, proof, pricing or next step.

**Images and assets:** The operator's own Spline scene and a poster of it. The team has never shipped real Spline, so this stays experimental.

**Animation and interaction:** Scene reacts to hover and clicks; interface buttons trigger scene events. Micro-interactions throughout.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Native scroll. The scene may react to scroll position through events.

**Responsive:** Poster on mobile unless the scene is verified light enough.

**Use for:** SaaS features; Micro-3D hero

**Avoid for:** Low-end device floors; Projects without a Spline account or scene

**Combines with:** nothing

**The render check requires:** webgl; forbids pinned

**From the team:** Workbook: Spline never used; Sketchfab GLB and procedural Three.js substituted. Skill: SplineScene behind a poster with events

**Interpretation:** Almost all design guidance: no team evidence yet

## APP-05 Shader / WebGL Website

The surface of the site is alive. A custom GPU-drawn material is the brand's visual signature, and everything else is restrained so it can breathe.

**Principles**

- One authored shader idea that belongs to this brand
- The effect expresses a concept: water for a port, heat for a foundry
- Type stays in the DOM and always readable
- The quality ladder is part of the design

**Visual identity:** Experiential and atmospheric: a living field of colour or texture with sparse, precise type over it. Studio-portfolio energy.

**Art direction:** Derive the shader from the brand concept and palette. Decide its scale, speed and grain on purpose, and repeat it in small doses across pages.

**Layout and composition:** Large immersive fields alternating with very quiet text sections. Sparse grids, big margins. Patterns: `full-bleed`, `statement`, `layered-field`, `list-editorial`, `overlap`.

**Typography:** Sharp display type with wide spacing or strong contrast over the field, plus a readability scrim where the field moves behind text.

**Colour:** Palette comes alive inside the shader; the interface stays nearly monochrome.

**Content:** Short and confident. Few words, strong statements, portfolio-like lists.

**Images and assets:** The shader is the main asset. Very few photos, treated to match the field.

**Animation and interaction:** Continuous slow motion in the field, reacting to pointer and scroll. Interface motion stays minimal.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Native scroll. Scroll may shift the shader's parameters. Only one canvas runs at a time.

**Responsive:** Quality ladder: full, reduced, then a CSS gradient or still frame. Text contrast is checked over the fallback too.

**Use for:** Creative studios; Experiential brands; Accent backgrounds for a brand with a strong concept

**Avoid for:** Content-heavy sites; Motion intensity 0

**Combines with:** APP-02 (The story has one shader scene as a chapter)

**The render check requires:** webgl; forbids pinned

**From the team:** Workbook: custom GLSL for globe, ocean, landscape; ocean static, morphing incomplete. Skill: ShaderBackground with a quality ladder. Taste docs: headline must not be painted by the shader; scrim over moving fields

**Interpretation:** Concept-derived shader, restraint rules

## APP-06 Game-Like Website

The visitor learns by playing. One bounded mechanic turns the message into something you do, and the explainer holds the same content for anyone who skips.

**Principles**

- One mechanic only
- Playing reveals the actual content
- Skip is always visible
- Completion leads to the call to action

**Visual identity:** A small invented world with its own rules, characters or tokens, with an interface styled as part of the game.

**Art direction:** Build a coherent little world: consistent sprite or shape language, sound on demand, score and progress as design elements.

**Layout and composition:** A stage section that dominates, then the explainer below with the same items in readable form. Patterns: `game-stage`, `statement`, `list-editorial`, `full-bleed`.

**Typography:** Characterful display type that fits the world; plain body type in the explainer.

**Colour:** A saturated, world-specific palette, with enough contrast for play.

**Content:** Content unlocks as items in the game, each with a short title and text mirrored in the explainer.

**Images and assets:** Authored sprites or shapes; licensed sound; everything recorded in the register.

**Animation and interaction:** Game physics and feedback: collect, unlock, celebrate. Keyboard and touch both work.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Scrolling is paused only while the visitor is actively playing and focus is on the stage.

**Responsive:** Touch controls and a smaller stage on mobile; fallback to the explainer on weak devices.

**Use for:** Branded games; Virtual showrooms; Only when the client confirms play is the point

**Avoid for:** Any brief where play is not the point

**Combines with:** nothing

**The render check requires:** game; forbids pinned

**From the team:** Workbook: no tools, demo or evidence yet. Skill: one bounded mechanic with progress, sound and skip

**Interpretation:** All design guidance: no team evidence yet

## APP-07 AI + 3D + Motion + Real Website

A flagship production: one world, told through cinematic scroll, anchored by a real-time 3D centrepiece, with real content and production discipline. The parts are one film, never a collage.

**Principles**

- One world and one concept across all parts
- The 3D object is the protagonist of the scroll story
- A shared performance budget
- Only one WebGL canvas at a time

**Visual identity:** Enterprise-flagship scale: a single monumental idea (a globe, an engine, a building) carried from the first screen to the last.

**Art direction:** Direct it like a film with a hero prop. Light, grade and type stay constant so scroll and 3D feel like one medium.

**Layout and composition:** Pinned chapters staged around the 3D centrepiece, relieved by quieter proof sections and a real multi-page structure. Patterns: `full-bleed`, `pinned-scene`, `object-stage`, `annotated-object`, `horizontal-story`, `statement`.

**Typography:** Monumental display type plus precise annotation labels.

**Colour:** A controlled cinematic grade that the 3D lighting also follows.

**Content:** A narrative for the flagship page, with full supporting pages for real business content.

**Images and assets:** One heavy hero asset within budget; the team hit load problems with several. Licensed models, poster frames for each chapter.

**Animation and interaction:** Camera moves tied to scroll chapters, overlays synced to camera, scrubbed reveals.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Lenis with ScrollTrigger; 3D paused when out of view.

**Responsive:** Drops to APP-01 plus APP-02 on weak devices; each 3D part falls back to its poster.

**Use for:** Enterprise flagships at tier L

**Avoid for:** Low-end device floors; Small budgets; Sites without one strong central idea

**Combines with:** APP-05 (A shader scene is one chapter of the same world)

**The render check requires:** pinned, webgl; forbids nothing

**From the team:** Workbook: 3D globe with shipping arcs and scroll camera, first version judged visually weak, heavy assets. Skill: composite of APP-02 and APP-03 with one budget and one canvas

**Interpretation:** One-world rule, hero prop direction

## APP-08 AI Image to Frame Animation to 3D

A still image comes to life under the scroll. One crafted visual sequence is the site's centrepiece, with a sense of depth impossible in flat layouts.

**Principles**

- One sequence with a clear beginning and end
- Provenance of every frame is on record
- Depth and parallax come from the image itself
- The key frame must be beautiful alone

**Visual identity:** A visual narrative: dreamlike or hyper-real imagery with a consistent generated or filmed look.

**Art direction:** Decide the sequence first: subject, transformation, camera path, then compose the page around it.

**Layout and composition:** A pinned full-viewport frame stage with captions that arrive at set frames, then quiet supporting sections. Patterns: `frame-stage`, `full-bleed`, `statement`, `overlap`, `chapter-opener`.

**Typography:** Editorial captions timed to frames, with large type only at the key moments.

**Colour:** Taken from the imagery, so the interface feels cut from the same film.

**Content:** Captions tied to moments in the sequence, then a short conventional section for details and the call to action.

**Images and assets:** 24 to 60 frames at most 720 px high and 3 MB in total, with dense keyframes when cut from video. No watermarks: the team found AI and stock marks in supplied assets.

**Animation and interaction:** Canvas-drawn scrubbed frames, depth-map parallax on pointer.

**Scrolling and transitions:** Pinned while the sequence plays; scroll position maps directly to the frame.

**Responsive:** A smaller frame set or the static key frame on mobile and low-end devices.

**Use for:** Visual narratives; Parallax heroes

**Avoid for:** Motion intensity 0; Low-end device floors; Assets without clear rights

**Combines with:** APP-02 (The sequence is the central scene of a longer scroll story)

**The render check requires:** pinned, canvas; forbids nothing

**From the team:** Workbook: frame scrub proven, depth-map untried, lag from sparse keyframes, watermarks in assets. Skill: FrameSequence and DepthParallax with provenance

**Interpretation:** Sequence-first direction
